Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 1 of 6
Budget & Finance Standing Committee
Thursday, November 19, 2026 – 5:30 p.m.
City Hall
1st Floor Council Conference Room
9 Dale Avenue
Gloucester, MA 01930
and via Zoom
-Minutes-
Present: Chair Councilor Scott Memhard; Councilor Jason Grow; Councilor Patti-Ann Page
Absent: Vice Chair Councilor Tony Gross
Also Present: CAO, Kelly Dolan; General Counsel, Suzanne Egan; Budget Specialist, Kevin Nunes;
Auditor, Kenny Costa (remote); DPW Director, Michael Hale; Planning Director, Gregg
Cademartori; Chair of Board of Health, Joseph Rosa
Meeting called to order at 5:30 p.m.
This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.
Councilor Memhard announced the names of the B&F Committee members in attendance and City staff
who were in attendance in person and on Zoom.
1. Memorandum from the City Auditor regarding adoption of the 3-year Snow & Ice 
Amortization Schedule.
Summary of Discussion: Auditor, Kenny Costa stated that in FY26 there had been a historic snow and
ice deficit of $6,338,684. He stated that the State was allowing the City to amortize the deficit for three
years, and the Committee needed to approve the schedule. He stated that the State would also be
reimbursing the City $1,205,038 of the deficit, making the net deficit that needed to be amortized $5.1
million. He stated that the amortization of the deficit was part of the State’s requirements for setting the
tax rate. 
Councilor Page asked for clarification regarding the tax rate requirement for the amortization. Kenny
Costa stated that if the deficit had been a smaller amount, then the City would have been required to raise
those funds during the tax recap. He stated that because it was a large amount the State was allowing for
an amortization schedule instead. 
Councilor Grow asked if there was any benefit to paying more of the deficit up front. Kenny Costa
stated that the amount of free cash the City would have after the books were closed had not been
determined yet. He stated that the amortization schedule could be changed in the future however. He
stated that the Department of Revenue required the City to complete the amortization schedule by 2029,
and if it was not, then the City would need to raise any remaining amount as part of the tax recap.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
approve the FY2026 Snow and Ice Deficit Amortization Schedule for FY27, FY28, and FY29 in
accordance with Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 101, Section 36 of the Acts of 2026.
Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 2 of 6
2. Memorandum from the Interim Police Chief requesting acceptance of a donation in the 
amount of $100 from the Massachusetts Elks Association to support any CIU program.
Summary of Discussion: None.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
accept a cash donation under MGL c. 44, §53A, to support Community Impact Unit in the amount of
$100 from the following member and business partner in our community:
NAME AMOUNT DATE
Massachusetts Elks Association Inc. $     100.00 09/27/26
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total $     100.00
3. Memorandum from the General Counsel requesting approval to pay FY2026 invoices with 
FY2027 funds.
Summary of Discussion: None.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
approve, in accordance with MGL c. 44, §64, payment of a prior year invoice for Registry of Deeds at
100 Cummings Center, Suite 206-C, Beverly, MA 01915 provided deed recording, for the purpose of
paying invoice #15773, invoice dated October 20, 2026, in the amount of $210 to be paid with the current
year FY2027 General Fund, Legal Department – Ordinary Maintenance budgeted funds.
4. Memorandum from the General Counsel requesting approval to pay FY2026 invoices with 
FY2027 funds.
Summary of Discussion: General Counsel, Suzanne Egan stated that Weston & Sampson provided
third-party review services to the Board of Health during the Eastern Waste public hearing. She stated
that the applicant had been required to pay for a percentage of the review, and anything more than that
percentage was the City’s obligation per State law. She stated that Weston & Sampson had testified during
the public hearing and had also helped write the conditions for the site. 
Councilor Page asked what the total amount that Weston & Sampson had charged. Suzanne Egan stated
that the applicant had paid $22,000 and the City $27,530.
Councilor Page asked for clarification on the applicant paying for the third-party review. Suzanne Egan
stated that under State law there were provisions that a permitting board can ask an applicant to pay for
third-party review. 
Councilor Page stated her concerns regarding the lack of detail for the traffic study for the train bridge
on Magnolia Avenue. Suzanne Egan stated that the review was done by traffic engineers that followed
the standards set out by the State. Chair of Board of Health, Joseph Rosa stated that the Board of Health
had to make their ruling on the facts that had been presented by experts. Suzanne Egan stated that the
decisions of the Board and the City had to be based on facts so they were defensible. Joseph Rosa stated
that the peer review had determined that the underpass was within safety standards.
Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 3 of 6
Councilor Page asked if the City could refuse to pay the traffic study portion of the invoice. Suzanne
Egan stated that the City was under contract and had to pay the obligation in full.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 2 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 present (Page), to recommend
that the City Council approve, in accordance with MGL c. 44, §64, payment of a prior year invoice
Weston & Sampson at Walkers Brook Drive, Suite 100, Reading, MA 01867 provided peer review
services that were provided during the Board of Health public hearing on the Eastern Waste Site
Assignment application, for the purpose of paying invoice #2260918, invoice dated February 12, 2026,
in the amount of $27,530 to be paid from various current year FY2027 General Fund accounts, including
Legal Department, Board of Health and Mayor’s Office – Ordinary Maintenance budgeted funds.
5. Memorandum from the Director of Public Works requesting acceptance of the revised FEMA
Public Assistance Grant in the amount of $510,910.
Summary of Discussion: DPW Director, Michael Hale stated the project had been ongoing since 2018,
and the City had been working to get more funds from FEMA, as their original estimate had been too
low. He stated that the funds were to repair the armored bank on Cressey’s Beach in Stage Fort Park. He
stated that the grant had to be extended seven times, and the City had till the end of the calendar year to
get to the project to substantial completion. He stated that there would be $170,000 of local money used,
and $383,182.50 of FEMA funds. He stated that there would be 400 feet of armored embankment
completed by contractors by the end of the calendar year, and the vegetation would be completed in June.
Councilor Grow asked for clarification on the armored bank. Michael Hale stated that stones would be
installed to protect the soil from eroding. He stated that the project had been approved by the Conservation
Commission, the Department of Environmental Protection, and the Army Corps of Engineers. 
Councilor Memhard asked if the mature trees on the embankment would be preserved. Michael Hale
stated that was the intention.
Councilor Page asked if the new armored embankment would extend further into the water. Michael
Hale stated that it would not.
Councilor Page asked where the additional $174,000 of City money was coming from. Michael Hale
stated that it would be coming from the DPW budget. 
Councilor Memhard made the following motion, however it was not seconded, and the Committee
unanimously voted to recommend the matter to City Council. 
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: The Committee moved to recommend that the City Council
accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA
Region 1), U.S. Department of Homeland Security in the amount of $383,182.50 for the purpose of
additional repairs to the Cressy Beach revetment. There is a $127,727.50 local matching requirement for
the grant and the period is from January 1, 2027 through April 30, 2028.
6. Memorandum from the Planning Director requesting acceptance of the LAND Grant award 
for the Magnolia Reserve Conservation project in the amount up to $425,000
Summary of Discussion: Chris LaPointe, President, Greenbelt, stated that Greenbelt and the City
would be entering into a partnership to permanently protect 94 acres of land on Magnolia Avenue.
Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 4 of 6
Planning Director, Gregg Cademartori stated that the conservation project was many years in the
making. He stated that there had been a number of development proposals for the property, and the
property had been included in two iterations of the Open Space Plan. He stated that it was a highly
valuable piece of property for conservation due to the habitats on the land, and it being contiguous with
other adjacent conserved land, which amounted to almost 1,000 acres including Ravenswood. He stated
that the Open Space Committee and the Conservation Commission unanimously supported the
conservation of the land. He stated that the Conservation Commission would be the holder of the
conservation restriction on the land, which is what the LAND grant would partially fund in the amount
of $425,000. He stated that there was a request for Community Preservation Act funds as well, in the
amount of $300,000. He stated a final small private donation from Greenbelt would make up the final
portion of the total cost. He stated that the total cost of the conservation restriction would be $759,000.
He stated that Greenbelt would be the owner of the property and the Conservation Commission would be
the holder of the conservation restriction. He stated that the cost of the conservation restriction to the
City was lower than the current appraised value of the conservation restriction.
Chris LaPointe stated that the $759,000 amount was 50% of the assessed value of a conservation
restriction on the property, which was a benefit to the City. He stated that the fundraising that Greenbelt
was doing to acquire the property was going well, and they had secured a $500,000 grant from Mass
Audubon. 
Councilor Grow stated that there were current development proposals for the site that included 26
duplexes. He stated that there were several adjacent lots that were owned by the City. 
There was a brief discussion regarding real property. It was determined that the conservation restriction
held the development rights of the property.
There was a brief discussion regarding the effect to the City’s taxes by removing the property from the
tax rolls. It was determined that the land produced about $9,200 a year in taxes.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a state grant from the Executive Office of Energy and Environmental
Affairs (EEA), Local Acquisitions for Natural Diversity (LAND) Grant in the amount of $425,000 for
the purpose of acquiring a permanent Conservation Restriction for the Magnolia Reserve Property (171
and 281R Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue.)  There are no local
matching requirements for the grant and the period is from November 1, 2026 through June 1, 2027.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor 
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City 
Council accept the Conservation Restriction for the Magnolia Reserve Property (171 and 281R 
Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue) as follows:
Ordered: That the Gloucester City Council hereby votes to:
1. Raise and appropriate the sum of $759,000, or such other amount as may be necessary, to 
acquire a perpetual Conservation Restriction, for the purposes of conservation, protection of 
wildlife habitat, preservation of natural resources, watershed protection, passive outdoor 
recreation, and open space, over approximately 94 acres of land known as the Magnolia 
Reserve Property (171 and 281R Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western 
Avenue), located in Gloucester, Massachusetts, together with all costs incidental and related 
thereto. Said Conservation Restriction shall be held by the Gloucester Conservation
Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 5 of 6
Commission pursuant to the provisions of Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 8C,
and Article 97 of the Amendments to the Massachusetts Constitution.
2. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, on behalf of the City, to acquire said 
Conservation Restriction by purchase, gift, bargain and sale, donation, or such other lawful 
means, upon such terms and conditions as the City determines to be in its best interest.
3. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, the Mayor, and such other municipal 
officers as may be necessary to apply for, receive, accept, administer, and expend grants, gifts, 
reimbursements, and other financial assistance from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, the 
United States Government, nonprofit organizations, and other public or private funding sources 
to defray all or a portion of the acquisition costs. Such funding shall include, but not be limited 
to, assistance available through the Land Acquisition for Local Diversity (LAND) Grant 
Program authorized under M.G.L. Chapter 132A, Section 11, and any successor or related 
federal or state conservation funding programs.
4. Authorize the Mayor, the Gloucester Conservation Commission, and other appropriate 
municipal officials to execute all applications, grant agreements, conservation restriction 
documents, certifications, deeds, and any other instruments or agreements necessary or 
convenient to complete the acquisition and fulfill all grant requirements.
5. Provided, however, that any municipal funds appropriated pursuant to this vote shall not be 
expended unless and until the City has secured all required matching funds, grants, gifts, or 
other contributions necessary to complete the acquisition in accordance with the approved 
project budget.
This authorization is intended to facilitate the permanent protection of the Magnolia Reserve Property 
as a significant natural resource for the benefit of the residents of Gloucester and the Commonwealth, 
preserving its ecological, scenic, watershed, habitat, and passive recreational values in perpetuity.
7. Memorandum from the Harbormaster requesting acceptance of the 2025 CVA Grant in the 
amount of $11,200
Summary of Discussion: Kenny Costa stated that this was a reoccurring grant and it was outside the
normal acceptance period of the grant. He stated that the grant for 2026 would also be coming before the
Committee. He stated that due to turnover at the Harbormaster’s Office, the grants had not been applied
for during the normal acceptance period.
There was a brief discussion regarding house boats, and their participation in the program.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor 
Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City 
Council accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a federal grant from Department of the Interior passed through 
the Division of Marine Fisheries, Clean Vessel Act Grant in the amount of $11,000 for the purpose of 
servicing resident and transient boaters of the City for the disposal of sewage from vessel holding tanks,
portable toilets, and shore side pump-out facility. The original grant period is from January 1, 2025 
through December 31, 2025, and there is an in-kind match of payroll expenses. The City has requested 
a grant extension for the expired grant.
8. Memorandum from the City Auditor regarding accounts having expenditures which exceed
their authorization & Auditor’s Report and other related business
Budget & Finance                               November 19, 2026                                     Page 6 of 6
Summary of Discussion: Kenny Costa stated that the total amount had decreased by $74,000. He stated
that the Community Development deficit should be cleared up soon. 
No motion offered.
MOTION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance
Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to adjourn at 6:40 p.m.
Submitted by: Lynds Jones, Legislative Aide.
Documents submitted at the meeting: None.
Matters appearing on the agenda that are to be continued: None.
Meeting Recording:  https://www.gloucester-ma.gov/1097/Past-Remote-Public-Meetings

1. Raise and appropriate the sum of $759,000, or such other amount as may be necessary, to acquire a perpetual Conservation Restriction, for the purposes of conservation, protection of wildlife habitat, preservation of natural resources, watershed protection, passive outdoor recreation, and open space, over approximately 94 acres of land known as the Magnolia Reserve Property (171 and 281R Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue), located in Gloucester, Massachusetts, together with all costs incidental and related thereto. Said Conservation Restriction shall be held by the Gloucester Conservation Commission pursuant to the provisions of Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 8C, and Article 97 of the Amendments to the Massachusetts Constitution.

2. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, on behalf of the City, to acquire said Conservation Restriction by purchase, gift, bargain and sale, donation, or such other lawful means, upon such terms and conditions as the City determines to be in its best interest.

3. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, the Mayor, and such other municipal officers as may be necessary to apply for, receive, accept, administer, and expend grants, gifts, reimbursements, and other financial assistance from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, the United States Government, nonprofit organizations, and other public or private funding sources to defray all or a portion of the acquisition costs. Such funding shall include, but not be limited to, assistance available through the Land Acquisition for Local Diversity (LAND) Grant Program authorized under M.G.L. Chapter 132A, Section 11, and any successor or related federal or state conservation funding programs.

4. Authorize the Mayor, the Gloucester Conservation Commission, and other appropriate municipal officials to execute all applications, grant agreements, conservation restriction documents, certifications, deeds, and any other instruments or agreements necessary or convenient to complete the acquisition and fulfill all grant requirements.

5. Provided, however, that any municipal funds appropriated pursuant to this vote shall not be expended unless and until the City has secured all required matching funds, grants, gifts, or other contributions necessary to complete the acquisition in accordance with the approved project budget.

This authorization is intended to facilitate the permanent protection of the Magnolia Reserve Property as a significant natural resource for the benefit of the residents of Gloucester and the Commonwealth, preserving its ecological, scenic, watershed, habitat, and passive recreational values in perpetuity.

### 7. Memorandum from the Harbormaster requesting acceptance of the 2025 CVA Grant in the amount of $11,200

**Summary of Discussion:** Kenny Costa stated that this was a reoccurring grant and it was outside the normal acceptance period of the grant. He stated that the grant for 2026 would also be coming before the Committee. He stated that due to turnover at the Harbormaster’s Office, the grants had not been applied for during the normal acceptance period.

There was a brief discussion regarding house boats, and their participation in the program.

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor Page, the Budget & Finance Committee voted, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council accept under MGL c. 44, §53A, a federal grant from Department of the Interior passed through the Division of Marine Fisheries, Clean Vessel Act Grant in the amount of $11,000 for the purpose of servicing resident and transient boaters of the City for the disposal of sewage from vessel holding tanks, portable toilets, and shore side pump-out facility. The original grant period is from January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, and there is an in-kind match of payroll expenses. The City has requested a grant extension for the expired grant.
